description:
Search by what is wanted (an item, a dish, a service, in any language) near `location`, default radius 15 miles, when the trade is not known.
Each business shows its best-fitting items first; `match.fit` says how well: exact (the thing and every asked property), likely (the thing, a property not stated), property (the thing with another quantity or colour), partial (only its main word), none. `nothing_fitting` says so when nothing does.
Conditions you pass come back per business as met / violated / unknown (time: open_then / closed_then / unknown): the item's price is not the total, opening hours are not a delivery time, being near is not being served.
No `location` and nothing fitting → an empty list, not unrelated businesses from anywhere.

detail.description: compact (default): the business, its 1–2 best offerings with prices and links, what can be done, and the date it was read — a few hundred bytes a card. full: everything, including images, the sentence each price was read from, variants, all four fulfilment modes with published areas, opening hours and per-field evidence. Ask for full only when the user has chosen a business and you need its delivery area or its hours.

fulfillment.description: HOW it must reach the user, and the four are different questions: delivery = brought to the address; pickup = the user collects; on_site = the user goes there (a salon chair, a dining room); at_customer = the business travels (a mover, a plumber). Default any. A business that has not published an answer is KEPT; one that ruled it out is dropped.

limit.description: How many BUSINESS CARDS to return. Default 10.

location.description: Where the user is, or where it must happen. A 5-DIGIT US POSTCODE IS BEST ("33139"): it is the only form a business’s own published delivery or service area can be matched against exactly, so a postcode gets you `how: "zips"` and a city name gets you a distance. A city ("Orlando, FL") or "lat,lng" also work. OPTIONAL IN NAME ONLY — without it nothing is measured and nothing is narrowed, and the answer comes back with `needs` carrying the question to put to your user. "near me" is not a location: ask which town.

max_price.description: The most the user will pay for ONE offering, in USD, compared against the lowest number the business published — so "from $45" passes "under $50". An offering priced on request is NOT filtered out: it comes back `price_type: "quote_only"`, because "they quote it" is an answer.

needed_by.description: When it has to happen: "today", "tomorrow", "tomorrow 9am", or an ISO date-time — WITH an offset (2026-10-31T14:00:00-04:00) if you know the user’s zone, because a business whose cut-off is on the RECIPIENT’s clock can only be judged against an offset you give.

only_independent.description: true = leave out chains (a business whose website serves several of the places found). Default false: a chain is kept as a name, a telephone and a website — it was never read, so it has no offerings — and its card says `chain: true`.

only_local.description: true = leave out marketplaces: a business whose shelf names places far from its own address (one local address, hundreds of listings in other cities and countries). Default false: a marketplace is kept, ranked lower, and its card says `marketplace: true` (the full card says why).

properties.description: THE OPEN LAYER AS A FILTER: facts a business publishes beyond price and availability — a capacity, a deposit, a duration, whether something is included. Three states per key: a published value that fits = confirmed; a published value that does not = refuted (left out, a fact); nothing published = unknown (KEPT, ranked lower, named in the card’s `unknown`). Ask for the user’s real conditions here instead of putting them in `query`: «for 8 people» is {key:"capacity",min:8}, «no deposit» is {key:"deposit",max:0}.

equals.description: the value must be this, as the page wrote it («included», «yes», 8)

exists.description: true = the business must publish this property at all

key.description: a property key this index has read — get_card lists the ones established for a niche under `established_properties`, and every card shows its own under `properties`

max.description: the value must be at most this (a number); max 0 = «none»

min.description: the value must be at least this (a number)

query.description: What the user wants, IN THEIR OWN WORDS AND THEIR OWN LANGUAGE: "red roses", "steakhouse", "funeral flowers", "movers 2 bedroom", "ramo de rosas", or the same question in a language not written in the Latin alphabet. Matched by MEANING as well as by words, through one multilingual model — so do NOT translate for us and do NOT list synonyms yourself. A place, a date, a budget and a delivery word may be left in (they are parsed out), but the fewer extra words the better the match.

radius_miles.description: How far the business may be, in miles. Default 15.

title: A match by meaning, for when the trade is not known — check its results on the cards
